name: a chat_id that cannot name a conversation is refused locally, before the wire

context.note: Every conversation id is minted by member-backend with the cnv_ prefix and msghub resolves a chat_id only through member-backend, so anything else is answered with code=400 invalid conversation id. Both plugins forward a chat_id chosen upstream (host target parser, channel directory, cron target, tool argument), so each guards its own outbound boundary. The rejected samples below are the shapes a prefix-only check lets through, each of which member-backend refuses.
context.idcode_note: The prefix alone is not enough: member-backend validates the full shape of every externally-visible id. The shape is <3 lowercase ascii letters>_<26 Crockford base32 chars>, exactly 30 chars, separator at index 3. Crockford's alphabet omits I, L, O and U; decoding is case-insensitive, so a lowercase body is accepted while the 3-char prefix must be lowercase. A prefix-only check still lets cnv_, cnv_<id>:thr_1 and cnv_<display name> reach the wire, where member-backend answers 400 and msghub logs an ERROR for a frame that never had a recipient.
